note: Analyst choices the user may set. A method instruction in the question beats the user's setting, which beats the default. 'applied' says where the setting takes effect: 'code' = the tools apply it; 'answer' = it is given to Claude as a rule and stated in the answer.

conventions.label: Figures for earlier years

options.latest: From the latest filing that reports the year (picks up restatements and reclassifications)
options.original: As originally reported, in that year's own 10-K or 10-Q

affects: every figure taken for a past period
conventions.source: Analyst practice. Comparative columns of a later filing carry restatements and reclassifications, so time series use them for comparability (CFA Program Curriculum, Level I, Financial Statement Analysis, 'Financial Reporting Quality' on restatements); point-in-time and audit work uses the figure as originally reported.

conventions.label: Actual versus guidance: precision of the actual

options.exact: The exact figure from the financial statements (73.03%)
options.guidance: Rounded to the precision the guidance was given in (73.0%)

conventions.source: Catalogue entry 'beat or miss versus guidance': use the exact figure from the financial statements, not the rounded headline. The rounded comparison is a common desk alternative when guidance itself is given to one decimal.

conventions.label: Guidance point compared against

options.midpoint: Midpoint of a guided range (the stated figure for one-sided guidance)

conventions.source: Sell-side convention (results compared with the midpoint of the guided range); catalogue entry 'beat or miss versus guidance'.

conventions.label: GAAP or adjusted, when the question does not say

options.both_gaap_first: Both, carried through to the result: the GAAP figure first, the company's adjusted (non-GAAP) figure beside it, each labelled
options.both_adjusted_first: Both, carried through to the result: the company's adjusted (non-GAAP) figure first, the GAAP figure beside it, each labelled

affects: earnings, EPS and margins where a company reports a GAAP and an adjusted figure
guidance, beat or miss, valuation multiples
conventions.source: SEC Regulation G and Regulation S-K Item 10(e): a non-GAAP measure must be reconciled to the GAAP measure, which is given equal or greater prominence. Analyst practice works mostly from the adjusted figure, so both are shown; the GAAP figure is the one defined the same way for every company.

conventions.label: Which guidance, when it was revised

options.latest: The latest guidance the company had given as of the date of the question, with the release named; earlier versions mentioned if it was revised
options.original: The first guidance given for the period

affects: guidance, beat or miss, anything built on a guided figure
conventions.source: Analyst practice: results and prices are measured against the most recent guidance in force (sell-side convention; catalogue entry 'beat or miss versus guidance'). The original guidance answers a different question: how the year went against the first plan.

conventions.label: Share count for market cap and EV

options.cover_page: Basic shares on the cover page of the 10-K/10-Q for the balance-sheet date (as of the cover-page date); every answer also states the figures on the reported diluted weighted-average shares
options.balance_sheet: Shares outstanding on the balance-sheet date

conventions.source: CFA Program Curriculum, Level II, Equity Valuation, 'Market-Based Valuation': market value of equity = price x shares outstanding; which count is analyst convention. The cover-page count (SEC Regulation S-K, latest practicable date) is the most recent count a filing gives. Since 5 Nov 2026 answers state both counts, diluted first (user decision); the diluted count is the company's reported weighted average for the period, not a treasury-stock-method count at the price date.

conventions.label: Short-term investments in enterprise value

options.exclude: Subtract cash and cash equivalents only

conventions.source: CFA Program Curriculum, Level II, Equity Valuation, 'Market-Based Valuation' subtracts cash and short-term investments; many desks subtract cash and equivalents only. This catalogue's default is cash and equivalents.

conventions.label: Operating leases in enterprise value

options.if_asked: Added as debt-like only when the question says so
options.always: Always added as debt-like (current + non-current lease liabilities)

conventions.source: Rating-agency lease adjustment (S&P Global Ratings, Moody's); under ASC 842 lease liabilities are on the balance sheet but outside debt, so including them is a choice.

conventions.label: Cash subtracted in net debt
conventions.source: CFA Program Curriculum, Level II, Equity Valuation, 'Market-Based Valuation' (cash and short-term investments); catalogue default cash and equivalents.

conventions.label: What free cash flow subtracts

options.capex_only: Operating cash flow less purchases of property and equipment
options.broad: Also capitalised software and intangible purchases and finance-lease principal

conventions.source: Company and analyst practice (CFO - capex); CFA defines FCFF/FCFE separately (Level II, 'Free Cash Flow Valuation').

conventions.label: Cash conversion denominator
conventions.source: No CFA definition; desk convention varies.

conventions.label: DCF discounting
conventions.source: CFA Program Curriculum, Level II, 'Free Cash Flow Valuation' (end-of-period); mid-year is an investment-banking variant (Rosenbaum & Pearl).

conventions.label: Stock-based compensation in unlevered FCF

options.add_back: Added back as a non-cash charge
options.subtract: Treated as a cash cost (not added back)

conventions.source: CFA Program Curriculum, Level II, 'Free Cash Flow Valuation' (non-cash charges added back); subtracting SBC is a desk variant.

conventions.label: Transaction value in M&A questions

options.announced: The deal value the announcement itself states (merger 8-K, press release, proxy); an enterprise value built from the target's balance sheet is shown as a labelled alternative
options.rebuilt_ev: Enterprise value rebuilt from the offer price and the target's balance sheet (equity value + debt - cash ...)

conventions.source: Precedent-transaction practice: deal tables quote the transaction value the parties announce, with multiples on that value; analyst training (Wall Street Prep, Breaking Into Wall Street) builds EV only when the question asks for enterprise value. Added 5 Nov 2026 after four precedent answers led with a rebuilt EV where the question meant the announced value.

conventions.label: 'Revenue' where a company reports total revenue and net sales

options.total_revenue: Total revenues, the top line of the income statement
options.net_sales: Net sales, excluding membership fees and other income

affects: revenue, growth and margin for companies with membership or other income beside net sales
conventions.source: US GAAP presentation (ASC 606 / Regulation S-X Rule 5-03): total revenues is the top line and is defined the same way across companies. House convention agreed with the product owner on 11 Nov 2026 after the benchmark comparison.

conventions.label: 'R&D expense'

options.company_funded: The research and development expense line on the income statement (company-funded)
options.with_customer_funded: Company-funded plus customer-funded research and development, where the company discloses the latter

affects: R&D, R&D intensity, pro forma margins without R&D
conventions.source: US GAAP (ASC 730): research and development expense is the company-funded amount charged to the income statement; customer-funded work sits in cost of sales and is disclosed separately. House convention agreed with the product owner on 11 Nov 2026 after the benchmark comparison.

conventions.label: 'Organic growth'

options.ex_deals: The company's own published organic growth figure; if it publishes none, growth excluding acquisitions and disposals (the continuing business)
options.combined: Both businesses combined in both periods (pro forma for the deal)

affects: organic growth, like-for-like growth around an acquisition
conventions.source: Non-GAAP measure under SEC Regulation G; company reconciliations in earnings releases. CFA Program Curriculum (Financial Statement Analysis): organic growth excludes the effect of acquisitions and divestitures. House convention agreed with the product owner on 11 Nov 2026 after the benchmark comparison.

conventions.label: EBITDA where minority partners own part of the business

options.whole_company: EBITDA of the whole consolidated company, including the share of minority (non-controlling) interests
options.attributable: EBITDA attributable to the company's own shareholders, after the minority share

affects: leverage, debt capacity, EV/EBITDA for companies with non-controlling interests
conventions.source: Credit and valuation practice: consolidated debt and enterprise value (which includes non-controlling interests) are compared with consolidated EBITDA (CFA Program Curriculum, Equity Valuation: enterprise value multiples). House convention agreed with the product owner on 11 Nov 2026 after the benchmark comparison.

conventions.label: An 'adjusted' measure the company does not publish

options.closest_published: The company's closest published measure, named as such, with the GAAP figure beside it; no adjustments of our own
options.gaap_figure: The GAAP figure only, saying the company publishes no adjusted one

affects: adjusted EBIT, adjusted NOPAT, adjusted ROA and the like when the company reports no such line
conventions.source: SEC Regulation G: a non-GAAP measure is the company's, with its reconciliation. Standard practice is not to construct adjustments the company has not made. House convention agreed with the product owner on 11 Nov 2026 after the benchmark comparison.

conventions.label: A list pooled from several sources

options.distinct_once: Each distinct item counted once; items that appear in more than one source are named
options.with_repeats: Every entry counted as listed, repeats included

affects: averages and medians across precedent transactions, comparables or holdings taken from more than one list
conventions.source: Statistical practice: an average over transactions or companies counts each once (CFA Program Curriculum, Quantitative Methods). House convention agreed with the product owner on 11 Nov 2026 after the benchmark comparison.

conventions.label: Value of debt
affects: debt exchanges, tender offers, recoveries, value to holders
conventions.source: Market convention: bonds are quoted and exchanged on a clean-price basis, accrued interest settled separately (CFA Program Curriculum, Fixed Income: full price and flat price). House convention agreed with the product owner on 11 Nov 2026 after the benchmark comparison.

conventions.label: Liquidity

options.company_stated: The company's own stated liquidity figure, unless the question spells out a formula (then the formula, with the company's figure beside it)
options.rebuilt: Rebuilt from cash, securities and undrawn facilities

conventions.source: The filing is the primary source: where the company states a total, it leads (SEC Regulation S-K Item 303, liquidity and capital resources). House convention agreed with the product owner on 11 Nov 2026 after the benchmark comparison.

conventions.label: 'Highest' or 'lowest possible' share price

options.close: The highest or lowest closing price

affects: worst-case and best-case returns, price ranges
conventions.source: Plain meaning of highest and lowest price; market data reports intraday high and low alongside the close. House convention agreed with the product owner on 11 Nov 2026 after the benchmark comparison.

conventions.label: 'Projected', 'expected' or 'guided' figures

options.guidance: The company's guidance or outlook; if it cannot be obtained, the answer says so first and gives a result on the actual to date, labelled as a stand-in
options.actual_to_date: The actual figure to date, labelled

affects: projected tax rates, expected margins, anything the question calls projected or expected
conventions.source: A projection is forward-looking information from the company (earnings release, call or presentation), not a reported actual. House convention agreed with the product owner on 11 Nov 2026 after the benchmark comparison.

conventions.label: Earnings per share: diluted or basic
conventions.source: US GAAP (ASC 260) requires both; valuation and company guidance use diluted (CFA Program Curriculum, Financial Statement Analysis: earnings per share). House convention agreed with the product owner on 11 Nov 2026 after the benchmark comparison.

conventions.label: 'Average balance' for interest or a preferred return

options.with_period_accrual: Average of the opening and closing balance, the closing balance including the period's own accrual, in every period
options.before_period_accrual: Average of the opening balance and the balance after the period's cash flows, before the period's own accrual, in every period

affects: interest on average debt, preferred returns in fund waterfalls, any rate applied to an average balance
conventions.source: Financial modelling practice: interest on the average of opening and closing balances, solved with the accrual included (the circular form used in LBO and fund models). House convention agreed with the product owner on 11 Nov 2026 after the benchmark comparison.
